A delivery truck was valued at \$65 000 when new. The value of the truck depreciates at a rate of 22 cents per kilometre travelled.

What is the value of the truck after it has travelled a total distance of 132 600 km?

solutions.latex:
The truck loses $22$ cents, that is $\$0.22$, for each kilometre travelled.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Depreciation} &= 132\,600 \times 0.22 \\ &= \$29\,172 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Value} &= 65\,000 - 29\,172 \\ &= \$35\,828 \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
A plumber leases equipment which is valued at \$60 000.

The salvage value of the equipment at any time can be calculated using either of the two methods of depreciation shown in the table.

\extable{300_q28_t1}

Under which method of depreciation would the salvage value of the equipment be lower at the end of 3 years? Justify your answer with appropriate mathematical calculations.

solutions.latex:
Straight-line method, using $S = V_0 - D_n$:
$$\begin{aligned}S &= 60\,000-3500\times 3\\ &= \$49\,500\end{aligned}$$
Declining-balance method, using $S = V_0(1-r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned}S &= 60\,000(1-0.12)^3\\ &= 60\,000(0.88)^3\\ &= \$40\,888.32\end{aligned}$$
Since $\$40\,888.32 < \$49\,500$:
$$\therefore\ \text{the declining-balance method gives the lower salvage value.}$$
criteria: Correctly calculates the salvage value using the declining-balance method, or equivalent merit
Attempts to calculate the salvage value using the declining-balance method, or equivalent merit

4426.stem: A company purchases a machine for \$50 000. The two methods of depreciation being considered are the declining-balance method and the straight-line method.

parts.latex:
For the declining-balance method, the salvage value of the machine after $n$ years is given by the formula

$$S = V_0 \times (0.80)^n,$$

where $S$ is the salvage value and $V_0$ is the initial value of the asset.
What is the annual rate of depreciation used in this formula?
Calculate the salvage value of the machine after 3 years, based on the given formula.

For the straight-line method, the value of the machine is depreciated at a rate of $12.2\%$ of the purchase price each year.

When will the value of the machine, using this method, be equal to the salvage value found in part (a) (ii)?

solutions.latex:
The formula is $S = V_0 \times (0.80)^n$, so each year the value is $80\%$ of the previous value.

The annual rate of depreciation is $100\% - 80\% = 20\%$.

Using the given formula with $V_0 = 50\,000$ and $n = 3$:
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 50\,000 \times (0.8)^3 \\ &= \$25\,600 \end{aligned}$$

Straight-line depreciation each year is $12.2\%$ of the purchase price.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Annual depreciation} &= 12.2\% \times 50\,000 \\ &= \$6100 \end{aligned}$$
The value after $n$ years equals the salvage value from part (a)(ii).
$$\begin{aligned} 25\,600 &= 50\,000 - 6100n \\ -24\,400 &= -6100n \\ n &= \dfrac{-24\,400}{-6100} \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ n = 4 \text{ years}$$
criteria: Finds the annual depreciated amount, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
An asset is depreciated using the declining-balance method with a rate of depreciation of $8\%$ per half year. The asset was bought for \$10 000.

What is the salvage value of the asset after 5 years?

solutions.latex:
The depreciation rate is per half year, so the number of periods in 5 years is $n = 5\times 2 = 10$.

Using the declining-balance formula $S = V_0(1-r)^n$ with $V_0 = 10\,000$ and $r = 0.08$:
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 10\,000\,(1 - 0.08)^{10} \\ &= 10\,000\,(0.92)^{10} \\ &\approx \$4343.88 \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

4520.stem:
The value, $V$, of the machine after $n$ years is given by the formula

$$V = 60000 \times 0.85^{n}$$

parts.latex: By what percentage rate will the machine depreciate annually?
Calculate the value of the machine after three years.
At the end of which year will the machine’s value first fall below $\$12\,000$?

solutions.latex:
The formula $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$ has $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$ as its multiplier.
$$\text{Depreciation rate} = 15\%$$

Test values of $n$ in $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$.
$$\begin{aligned} n=8:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^8 = \$16\,349.43 \\ n=10:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^{10} = \$11\,812.46 \end{aligned}$$
The value is below $\$12\,000$ at $n=10$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the value first falls below } \$12\,000 \text{ at the end of year } 10$$
criteria: Substitutes values of $n$ to show the value crossing $\$12\,000$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source only tests n=8 and n=10; n=9 gives about $13\,897$, not shown in source, so 'first' year relies on that. Not added.

parts.latex:
Office furniture depreciates by the declining balance method at a rate of $13\dfrac{1}{3}\%$ per annum.

What is the value of office furniture that was purchased 5 years ago for \$15 000?

solutions.latex:
Declining balance: $S = V_0(1-r)^n$, with $r = 13\dfrac{1}{3}\% = \dfrac{2}{15}$, $V_0 = 15\,000$ and $n = 5$.

$$\begin{aligned} S &= 15\,000\left(1-\dfrac{2}{15}\right)^5 \\ &= 15\,000\left(\dfrac{13}{15}\right)^5 \\ &\approx \$7334 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the value is } \$7334 \text{ (option C)}$$

parts.latex:
Jaime bought a van for \$31 000 to make deliveries to customers. He applied a straight-line method of depreciation to the van.

After 3 years, the value of the van is \$19 000.

What was the annual amount of depreciation?

solutions.latex:
Let $D$ be the annual depreciation. After 3 years the value is the cost less $3D$.
$$\begin{aligned} 19\,000 &= 31\,000 - 3D \\ -12\,000 &= -3D \\ D &= \$4000 \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, the total depreciation is $31\,000 - 19\,000 = 12\,000$, so
$$12\,000 \div 3 = \$4000$$
$$\therefore\ D = \$4000 \text{ per year}$$
criteria: Correct substitution or difference of $12\,000$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Three years ago an appliance was valued at $\$2467$. Its value has depreciated by 15% each year, based on the declining-balance method.

What is its salvage value today, to the nearest dollar?

solutions.latex:
Under declining-balance depreciation the value after $n$ years is $S = V_0(1-r)^n$, with $V_0 = 2467$, $r = 0.15$ and $n = 3$.
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 2467(1-0.15)^3\\ &= 2467(0.85)^3\\ &\approx \$1515 \end{aligned}$$
The answer is D.

parts.latex:
Adam purchased some office furniture five years ago. It depreciated by $\$2300$ each year based on the straight-line method of depreciation. The salvage value of the furniture is now $\$7500$.

Find the initial value of the office furniture.

solutions.latex:
After 5 years the value is the initial value less $5$ years of depreciation.
$$7500 = V_0 - 5\times 2300$$
$$\begin{aligned} V_0 &= 7500 + 5\times 2300 \\ &= \$19\,000 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Initial value} = \$19\,000$$
criteria: Correct substitution into $S=V_0-Dn$, or equivalent merit

\exfigure{40_q29_1}

For the first 4 years, the value of the asset depreciated by \$1500 per year, using a straight-line method of depreciation.

After the end of the 4th year, the method of depreciation changed to the declining-balance method at the rate of $35\%$ per annum.

What is the total depreciation at the end of 10 years?

solutions.latex:
Straight-line depreciation for 4 years at $\$1500$ per year:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Depreciation} &= 1500 \times 4 \\ &= \$6000 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Value after 4 years} &= 50\,000 - 6000 \\ &= \$44\,000 \end{aligned}$$
For the next 6 years (years 5 to 10), the declining-balance method at $35\%$ gives $S = V_0(1-r)^n$ with $V_0 = 44\,000$, $r = 0.35$, $n = 6$:
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 44\,000(0.65)^6 \\ &\approx \$3318.43 \end{aligned}$$
Total depreciation is the original value minus the final value:
$$\begin{aligned} 50\,000 - 3318.43 &\approx \$46\,681.57 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the total depreciation is about } \$46\,682.$$
criteria: Finds the value after 10 years, or equivalent merit
